newsitem.title: USA: US Army sex case witness 'betrayed' by co-accuser.
newsitem.headline: US Army sex case witness 'betrayed' by co-accuser.

text.p: A Navy woman alleging sexual misconduct by the Army's highest-ranking enlisted man testified on Tuesday that she felt betrayed because the initial accuser has refused to take the witness stand along with other alleged victims.

The initial accuser, Sgt. Maj. Brenda Hoster, took her complaints against Sergeant Major of the Army Gene McKinney to the media last February, prompting three other women to come forward with allegations of past misconduct by McKinney.
But Hoster has refused to testify in order to avoid a bruising cross examination of her personal life by defence attorneys, Hoster's lawyer said in a letter.
"I do feel a little betrayed by it," Navy Petty Officer First Class Johnna Vinson said of Hoster's refusal. "I came forward to support her."

McKinney, a popular and charismatic chief advocate for the Army's enlisted soldiers, is accused of groping one female solider inside his Pentagon office and pressuring another into unwanted sex while she was nearly eight months pregnant.
McKinney faces 18 charges of sexual misconduct including indecent assault, adultery and obstruction of justice. He vigorously denies all the charges.
The hearing's purpose is to determine whether McKinney, a 29-year Army veteran, must face a court-martial.
Hoster's lawyer on Monday said her client refused to testify because of the way defence lawyers were grilling other accusers about intimate details of their personal lives.
McKinney's lead defence attorney, Charles Gittins, has told reporters Hoster would face questions about an alleged lesbian affair she had with another soldier.

Hoster's former barracks roommate, retired Sgt. Maj. Elizabeth D. McCullum, has given a sworn statement to Army investigators alleging she witnessed Hoster and another female soldier naked together in bed. McCallum also said Hoster confided that she loved the other woman, who is now under investigation by the Army.

Hoster's lawyer, Susan Graham Barnes, sent a letter to prosecutors saying she would not allow her client to participate in a "process which appears to have the purpose of punishing the alleged victims for making their complaints against SGM McKinney."
Hoster, now retired, could be forced to testify in the hearing if she is called back to active duty.
